newsitem.title: BELARUS: Belarus orders out Russian journalist.
newsitem.headline: Belarus orders out Russian journalist.

text.p: Belarus has ordered a reporter for a Russian television network to leave the former Soviet republic in the next four days, Belarus state television said on Thursday.
A television presenter reading from a foreign ministry statement said Alexander Stupnikov, a correspondent for the Russian commercial network NTV, should leave by March 31.
The decision was the latest action against foreign reporters in Belarus since hardline President Alexander Lukashenko accused foreign media of bias in reporting opposition protests.
The foreign ministry statement said Stupnikov's actions as chief of the NTV bureau in Minsk had undermined good neighbourly relations between Russia and Belarus, who are close allies.

Stupnikov had already had his accreditation withdrawn and NTV had asked the Russian government to "stop the persecutions of Russian journalists in Belarus" and described the attacks on him as arbitrary.
President Boris Yeltsin expressed concern on Tuesday about the problems facing Russian journalists in Belarus and asked the authorities in Minsk to guarantee media freedoms.
Journalists in Minsk were prevented last Sunday from entering the main television centre where they usually transmit their reports.

Lukashenko is due to visit Moscow on Friday for a summit of the leaders of the 12-nation Commonwealth of Independent States. He had been due in Moscow on Thursday but he postponed his arrival by a day.
Lukashenko is due to meet Yeltsin on a separate trip to Moscow on April 2 to sign a treaty on closer ties based on a "commonwealth" of two states on which they agreed on April 2 last year.
